A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Markov-VAR work. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and references are readable and support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; v3's additional page contains the end of the bibliography.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet generation results, efficiency measurements, history-compensation and window-size ablations, and scaling analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results, including the Markov-VAR measurements in Tables 1–5 and the accompanying analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Markov-state formulation, sliding-window history compensation, cross-attention aggregation, state concatenation, teacher-forcing procedure, and cross-entropy objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K for class-conditional image generation, retaining the same 256×256 quantitative generation benchmark, higher-resolution visualizations, and efficiency evaluations through 1024×1024. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and Figure 7. The newly discussed MVAR by Zhang et al. is not added to any experimental comparison and is distinct from Ren et al.'s M-VAR baseline already present in Table 1.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation metrics. Table 3 retains the H200 efficiency protocol with batches of 25; the ablation settings and depth-6-to-24 scaling evaluation are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The history-compensation alternatives in Table 4, window sizes 1–4 in Table 5, perturbation and cross-scale analyses in Figure 2, memory and scaling analyses in Figures 4–5, and qualitative examples in Figures 6–7 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both Table 3 captions report peak memory averaged over five runs, and Figure 5 retains the same fit statistics. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a revised uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain all result entries and numerical values, and the figures retain the same plotted findings and generated samples. For example, depth-16 FID remains 3.61 for VAR versus 3.23 for Markov-VAR, and depth-24 memory at 1024×1024 remains 117.9 versus 19.1 GB.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the sufficient-statistic argument, and the mathematical definitions of the history window and dynamic state are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about Markovian scale prediction, history compensation, improved generation and efficiency, and model-weight release. The additional prior-work discussion does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 changes the conclusion that Markov-VAR 'preliminarily follows the expected scaling law on model size' to 'follows the expected scaling law,' removing an explicit qualification without changing the evidence. The main mechanism interpretations and ImageNet-quality caveat remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture details, tokenizer, optimizer, learning rate, batch-size and epoch ranges, and training/evaluation hardware are unchanged. Both versions provide the same project-page link and model-weight release statement, with no additional reproducibility or access information.

R1.justification: V3 adds nine bibliography entries, including MVAR, EasyText, Fonts, WordCon, and MakeAnything. Section 2 adds a focused discussion of MVAR's spatial-Markov attention and emphasizes historical-information preservation, concise modeling, and scaling validation; the broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 locally revises the related-work paragraph, shortens the scaling and generation-process discussion, corrects spacing in the conclusion, and adds project-lead/corresponding-author footnotes. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All seven figures and five tables are retained. Figure 4 moves above Table 5 on page 7, while the author footnote and expanded bibliography produce local reflow, including a nearly empty final references page. These are limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: Acknowledging MVAR improves coverage of closely related work. However, some new citations appear mismatched to their supporting statements: EasyText's listed title describes diffusion-based text rendering, yet it supports autoregressive text generation; MakeAnything's diffusion-transformer title accompanies the VQ autoregressive synthesis discussion. V3 also removes the preliminary qualification from unchanged scaling evidence. With the scientific content otherwise stable, these mixed editorial effects do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
